items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Jerry was managing Harry James, and he said, 'Well, you got to sign these options.

ctx.x: I'll never forget it, though, he gave me a picture -- I lost that picture back in 1955; somebody stole my belongings, because I had messed up; if they didn't steal them then I left them there, never did find them misplaced them. But I moved out of this room, -- but I remember that; we went out that night, and oh my God, we played, we sang "The Lamp is Low" -- I'll never forget the routine we did. "The Lamp is Low" -- we did "The Sheik of Arabee" and we closed with "Tiger Rag" which we used as a flash, and we…

Jerry was managing Harry James, and he said, 'Well, you got to sign these options. We're gonna take you out to Victor Hugo's out in the West Coast.' He says, 'We're gonna give you a couple of jobs playing up there -- at the Hotel Sherman -- for smokers.' However, we signed these options and we went down there a couple of times; they had a couple of jobs while the band was still there.

And when it was time for them to leave, he had to explain that he wouldn't accept no colored out at Victor Hugo's. But we were talented, and that group broke up right then. And somebody come by my house when I was staying with Reverend Turner and said, 'You want to go to Quincy, Illinois?' A trumpet player named Roy something -- I can't remember too well, but we went down there. Our piano player at that time was Bill Samual, with Roy's trumpet player, and alto player and a drummer, and myself -- and we had a girl…
